faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Our Hispanic Clinic
faq.subtitle: Answers to common questions about our medical services in Houston
faq.q1: How does showing up at Clínica Hispana Cruz #3 without a reservation work?
faq.a1: Come in off S Braeswood, give your name at the front desk, and you're checked in on a first-come, first-served basis. There's no time slot to reserve by phone or online. Bringing a photo ID and a list of the medications you take makes check-in go more smoothly.
faq.q2: I'm uninsured. How do I pay for my visit?
faq.a2: We see patients with or without insurance. If you don't have a plan, you pay the clinic directly with cash or a debit or credit card. Interested in a women's or men's checkup package? Ask the front desk for the current price or look at the promotions section of this site.
faq.q3: Will my diagnosis and instructions be explained in Spanish or English?
faq.a3: Spanish is the clinic's main language, so check-in, your visit and your treatment instructions all happen in Spanish with no interpreter in between. We also see patients in English, which helps when kids or partners in the family are more at ease speaking it.
faq.q4: Are you open on Saturdays and Sundays, and what are the hours?
faq.a4: We're open seven days a week, weekends included, from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM. Those long hours let you stop by before your shift, on your lunch break or after work in the evening. Holiday schedules can shift, so a quick WhatsApp note before heading over on those dates saves you a wasted trip.
faq.q5: What kinds of health problems do you treat at the Braeswood location?
faq.a5: We offer general medical visits and ongoing care for chronic conditions such as diabetes, high blood pressure and cholesterol, plus allergies, thyroid problems, respiratory infections, vaccines, EKGs and ultrasound. Minor procedures like stitches, abscess drainage and ingrown toenail treatment are done here too. The full list is on our services page.
faq.q6: Can I get my I-693 immigration medical exam here?
faq.a6: Yes. The clinic has a USCIS-designated Civil Surgeon for the medical exam that goes with a Green Card application. Bring a photo ID and your vaccination record. Any vaccines you're missing can be given at the clinic as part of the process, based on what the exam shows.
faq.q7: I drive a commercial truck. Do you do the DOT physical for my CDL?
faq.a7: Yes, we perform the Department of Transportation physical required for CDL drivers. It covers vision, hearing, blood pressure and a urine sample. Wear whatever corrective lenses or hearing devices you normally drive with, and if diabetes or hypertension is part of your history, recent readings or notes from your regular provider help the exam go smoothly.
faq.q8: Can I get blood and urine tests done without going to a separate lab?
faq.a8: Yes, samples are collected right at the clinic. Blood work includes glucose, A1C, cholesterol and thyroid tests, and we also run urinalysis, stool tests and screening for sexually transmitted infections. The medical team goes over your results with you, explains what they mean and lays out the next step.
faq.q9: What does basic gynecological care for women include?
faq.a9: Basic gynecology here covers Pap smears, checks for discharge or intimate discomfort, pregnancy testing, birth control counseling and removal of contraceptive implants. If your situation calls for a specialist, the clinic's medical team guides you through the referral so you know exactly where to go next.
faq.q10: Can my kids get the physical their school asks for?
faq.a10: Yes, we see children and do the school physical that many Houston schools require. Bring the form the school gave you, your child's vaccination record and their glasses if they wear them. The medical team completes its section of the form and lets you know if any vaccine is missing.
faq.q11: Is parking free, and can I get in with a wheelchair?
faq.a11: Parking is free. The entrance and restrooms are wheelchair accessible, so older adults and people with limited mobility can get to their visit comfortably.
faq.q12: Where exactly is the clinic, and how can I ask questions before coming in?
faq.a12: We're at 5411 S Braeswood Blvd, Houston, TX 77096, in the Meyerland area, a short drive from Bellaire, Westbury and Fondren. We're one of the four Clínica Hispana Cruz locations in Houston. If you have questions about a service or what to bring, message us on WhatsApp before your visit.

location.about: Clínica Hispana Cruz #3 is a walk-in medical clinic at 5411 S Braeswood Blvd, Houston, TX 77096, in southwest Houston, in the Meyerland area near Bellaire and Westbury. It is open every day from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM and sees patients with or without health insurance, with self-pay by cash or card. Visits are in Spanish, and the staff also speaks English. The medical team provides family medicine, diabetes, blood pressure and cholesterol care, basic gynecology, lab work, ultrasound, EKG, DOT physicals, vaccines, stitches and the I-693 immigration medical exam with a USCIS-designated Civil Surgeon. There is free parking, a wheelchair-accessible entrance and restroom, and WhatsApp for questions. It is one of the four Clínica Hispana Cruz locations in Houston; the others are on Airline Dr (Cruz), Kuykendahl Rd (Cruz 2) and Beechnut St (Cruz 4).
